articleTitle: Time Division Duplexing for Enhanced Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer via Backscattering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In the ever-evolving digital landscape, Internet of Things (IoT) devices are transitioning from battery reliance to functioning as battery-less systems. This shift has led to innovative energy- and data-transfer methodologies. In this context, we introduce a Local Oscillator (LO)-less Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)-backscatter duplexing system that capitalizes on time-division duplexing (TDD) to enable the coexistence of SWIPT and backscatter modes. By employing TDD integration, switching mechanisms, and rectification processes, we achieve energy harvesting totaling 30.18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{J}$</tex> (equivalent to 57.37% of the node's harvested energy), all while maintaining a narrow operating bandwidth during both uplink and downlink communications. Remarkably, this results in a notable enhancement of the energy-harvesting efficiency and spectral utilization of battery-less nodes.

articleTitle: Space Sampling Techniques Comparison for a Synthetic Low-Pass Filter Bayesian Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of three sampling techniques for generating space points to develop a Bayesian neural network (BNN) surrogate model of a synthetic second-order low-pass filter. The objective is to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of different sampling methods in the performance of the Bayesian surrogate model. The study draws inspiration from widely used sampling techniques such as uniform distribution, uniformly distributed random numbers, and Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS). The results reveal that the BNN surrogate model achieves the best performance when using the LHS sampling method highlighting the impact of sampling techniques on the surrogate model's performance.

articleTitle: Neural Network Learning Techniques Comparison for a Multiphysics Second Order Low-Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: The design process of high frequency (HF) structures has been a major challenge in recent years, with the increasing demand for better performance and more complex designs. This process is even worse when considering multiphysics simulation, such as thermal and mechanical physics combined with the electromagnetic response of the circuit. The traditional approach of trial and error can be highly time consuming and prone to error while the use of direct optimization techniques can also be computationally expensive. To speed up the design process, artificial neural networks (ANN) have been extensively used to develop fast and accurate surrogate models of high-frequency structures. In this work, we compare the performance of three ANN learning techniques (Levenberg-Marquardt, Bayesian, and Resilient) for modeling a multi-physics second order low-pass filter implemented in COMSOL. Results demonstrate that the Bayesian ANN exhibits the best performance for efficiently and accurately model the multi-physical response of HF structures.

articleTitle: SAR Estimations in a Child Due to RF Exposures from Several Laptops in a Classroom Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This research provides a detailed examination of the exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMF) in a classroom environment. The study is driven by the escalating integration of electronic devices in educational settings and the subsequent necessity to estimate the implications of this on the overall exposure. The employed methodology simulates a classroom filled with several 7-year-old girls realistic models, each using a laptop, which are the primary sources of electromagnetic radiation. The 1g and 10g peak spatial Specific Absorption Rate (psSAR) are calculated for various parts of the child model, including the head, back, and hands. It is observed that, when several laptops are used, the psSAR can be substantially increased (e.g. up to 40-fold). One objective of this study is to enhance the understanding of potential EMF exposure effects in relation to age and to provide guidelines for the design of safer classrooms in the context of widespread laptop usage.

articleTitle: A Ka-band Electromagnetic Absorber based on Loaded Ring Slots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a frequency-selective absorber based on resistive loaded ring slots. The absorber consists of two layers separated by a dielectric substrate. One layer contains periodic annular ring slots loaded with four lumped resistors symmetrically distributed along the ring, while the second layer consists of a metallic screen. Simulation results show that the designed Ka-band absorber provides an absorption coefficient higher than 0.9 from 31.8 to 34.1 GHz and is suitable for both linear and circular polarizations of the incident electromagnetic wave.

articleTitle: Frequency-Selective Surface that Blocks Different WLAN Bands Based on Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Many safety-sensitive Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) applications rely on crowded frequency bands for short-range communication. In this context, Frequency-Selective Surfaces (FSSs) enlarge the space of possibilities to solve new Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) challenges through intelligent design. In this paper, we propose and test an FSS that is able to select between 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz signals based on polarization. Our low-cost, hand-made prototype is mechanically flexible, what expands the FSS range of uses. The measured transmission from 2.27 to 2.8 GHz is below −10 dB for vertically polarized waves and above −1 dB for horizontally polarized ones. The contrary happens from 5.45 to 5.96 GHz, with transmission above −1 dB and below −10 dB for vertical and horizontal polarizations, respectively.

articleTitle: Construction and Design of a 3.5 GHz Multi-Beam Antenna Using Butler Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In this paper, the design, modeling and characterization of a 4x4-element Butler matrix with an array of patch antennas connected to the four outputs of the Butler matrix is performed. A prototype 4x4-element Butler matrix with a linear array of 1x4 patch antennas on an FR-4 epoxy dielectric substrate with a thickness of 1.6 mm is designed and fabricated. Some key parameters of the Butler matrix, including magnitude and phase responses, are characterized and investigated by several measurements. The characterization results show that the 4x4 element Butler array and linear patch antenna array has a size of 150 mm by 235 mm and shows good magnitude and phase performances. The 3.5 GHz frequency is taken for the design, achieving the average measured phase difference between the output ports of almost 45°.

articleTitle: Determination of the Relative Permittivity and Loss Tangent of Liquid Samples Using a Miniature Low-Cost Microwave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In this paper we present the design of a compact low-cost microwave sensor and a method to determine the relative permittivity and loss tangent of liquid samples. The experiments have been done using full-wave simulations. The microwave sensor is built on a PLA substrate and copper adhesive tape, and its total size is 3,324.35 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The determination of relative permittivity is done by curve-fitting based on the shift of the loaded resonant frequency with respect to the unloaded resonant frequency of the sensor, whereas the loss tangent is predicted from the data obtained from the normalized difference in areas of the reflection coefficient, referred to the response of the sensor with a lossless sample. The sensor can respond in a stable way even with high loss-tangents, and low or high relative permittivity samples, as is the case with most liquids.

articleTitle: PCIe Gen6 Physical Layer Equalization Tuning by Using Unsupervised and Supervised Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Ever faster applications triggered the development of the new PCIe Gen6 specification, reaching 64 GT/s data rates with PAM4 modulation. This brings new challenges for the physical channel design, where equalization (EQ) plays a key role. PCIe specification defines an EQ process at the transmitter (Tx) and the receiver (Rx). Current post-silicon validation practices consist of finding optimal subsets of Tx and Rx coefficients by measuring the eye diagram at the Rx across many different channels. However, these practices are very time consuming since they require massive lab measurements. In this paper, we propose machine learning techniques to cluster post-silicon data from different channels and feed those clusters to Gaussian process regression (GPR) models. We then optimize each GPR surrogate to obtain the optimal tuning settings for each identified cluster. Our methodology is validated by using MATLAB SerDes Toolbox simulations of the functional eye diagram of a Gen6 link.

articleTitle: Microwave Intermediate Frequency (IF) Subsystem for Potential Nanosatellite and Space Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In wireless microwave communications schemes, heterodyne subsystems are normally used, taking advantage of the improved performance when compared to more basic direct detection and demodulation schemes. Heterodyne microwave communication schemes are based on two complementary subsystems: Intermediate frequency (IF) and high-frequency up/down conversion. In terrestrial, satellite and space communications, heterodyne schemes are preferentially used. In such a perspective, in this work, de design, realization and characterization of an IF subsystem for wireless communications, in particular focused to nanosatellites (CubeSats of 3 to 6 units) operating in the near-earth telecommunications X-band (7190–7235 GHz), is reported. The developed IF subsystem operates at a center frequency of 1.1 GHz, covering a band of at least 300 MHz. The IF subsystem feeds a modulated subcarrier to the up-conversion subsystem for generating a 7.2 GHz up-link microwave carrier The proposed IF subsystem includes the design of an IF PLL-based oscillator at 1.1 GHz and a quadrature modulator as a starting configuration for analog and digital communications capabilities.

articleTitle: Experimental Coverage Measurements on a Commercial 5G Network in the 28 GHz mm-Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents the coverage measurements and path loss results of a 5G indoor and outdoor signal within the 5G Laboratory located in the Department of Electrical Engineering of the University of Chile. An Ericsson AIR 5121 antenna and commercial base station that is in a fixed position inside the laboratory and a 5G router equipment (5G NR mmWave Mobile Hotspot) are used to perform measurements in the 28 GHz frequency band. Both Line of Sight (LoS) indoor and Non-Line of Sight (NLoS) scenarios were considered within the laboratory and in a hall next to the it and Line of Sight (LoS) outdoor the laboratory. The measurement results show acceptable data rates in DL and UL, however a deviation of 20 dB to 30 dB with respect to the 3GPP TR 38.901, METIS and NYU model. These results are expected to be important to review the coverage behavior of a commercial 5G network at the 28 GHz band millimeter wave frequency.

articleTitle: Coupled-Ladder Reflectionless Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This presentation will describe the circuit manipulations required to convert a well-known Cauer, or ladder topology filter prototype, to a coupled-ladder reflectionless filter prototype, without compromising the optimal transmission response and achieving theoretically perfect impedance match at both ports and at all frequencies. This relatively recent solution to a circuit design problem dating back almost 100 years (referred to then as constant-resistance networks) has sparked a resurgence in interest in absorptive filtering techniques. Practical implementations of coupled-ladder reflectionless filters ranging from discrete lumped-elements to monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) have produced low-pass, high-pass, and band-pass filters operating from the HF to mm-wave bands, and recognition of their advantages has led to increasing adoption as the preferred solution in a number of real-world applications.

articleTitle: Frequency-Selective Rasorber with Tunable Passband Based on Loaded Rings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with a tunable passband between two absorptive bands. The X-band FSR consists of two layers separated by an air gap. One layer is an absorptive surface designed by resistive-loaded meandered rings, and the second layer is a bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) realized with capacitive-loaded ring slots. Simulation results show that the central frequency of the passband decreases from 11.22 to 9.12 GHz as the capacitive load increases from 0.030 to 0.065 pF. The FSR design was validated using the waveguide simulator method. A demonstrator containing two unit cells was designed, fabricated and tested. The capacitive loading was implemented using interdigital capacitors to obtain a frozen state of the tunable FSR. There is a good agreement between simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Reduced Length Linear Tapered Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Tapered Slot antennas have the capability to operate in the ultra-wide band (UWB). Various studies examining their structural characteristics have revealed specific operational conditions. Moreover, it has been deduced that their performance tends to be less optimal at lower frequencies. Additionally, their large physical dimensions pose challenges for various applications. Consequently, the primary objective of this research is to propose a solution that can reduce the antenna's size while optimizing its maximum directivity. To achieve this goal, we conducted an analysis of different antenna designs. Through simulation, we determined that it is possible to achieve an antenna length of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.5}\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> with a corresponding directivity of 5.55 within a 0.75 directivity bandwidth (frequency band where the directivity is at least half of its maximum).

articleTitle: Low-Cost, High-Stability Arbitrary Clock Source Using Software GNSS Drift Correction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Clock drift is a major challenge for most RF systems in the field. There are many different solutions to obviate or compensate clock drift in these applications, though most are very complex and expensive. In this publication we present an arbitrary clock source, that uses a hybrid phase-locked loop concept to compensate drift of an oven-controlled oscillator by using an integrated clock synthesizer circuit. This allows for a cost effective design, that can use global satellite navigation systems, internal and external temperature sources, an aging model and automatic frequency control information from RF transceivers as an error correction source for the clock drift.

articleTitle: Hybrid Sensing and Communications Receiver Front-End for Mobile Communications Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This work introduces a mobile network front-end based on a direct sampling architecture, enabling simultaneous sampling of all frequency bands below 6 GHz used for mobile communications. Good channel isolation properties of above 43 dB for most channels are an essential enabler for future sensing and communications applications. Variable amplification within individual channels enables direct control over reception levels, and enhances resistance against willful and unwilling jamming of the receiver system.

articleTitle: Application of a Corner Reflector to Reduce the Dispersion of the OAM Beam of a Compact Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In this paper was presented a low-profile circularly polarized fractal antenna designed to generate an orthogonal OAM beam for vehicular communication system application at 5.9 GHz band. A Koch fractal geometry was designed using a code written in Scilab™. The final antenna design was achieved after implementation of the L-system together with a conformal transformation. A circularly polarized beam presenting OAM was obtained by applying a rotated rectangular patch rotated behind the fractal element. The collimation beam of the OAM fields is improved using a corner reflector behind the antenna with fractal element. The simulated of the resonant and radiation parameters of the proposed fractal antenna using the corner reflector were obtained using CST commercial software. The results shown a great a potential to control the long range performance in vehicular communication system using collimated OAM beam.

articleTitle: PCB Auto Routing Algorithm Based on Morphological Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Routing between electronic components in modern printed circuit boards (PCBs) is a complex task that requires manual work and can take months to accomplish. Auto-routers are a way to speed-up the PCB design process by automatically generating signal routings between components in a PCB. However, current state-of-the-art commercial solutions are not yet robust enough to create acceptable traces. This research proposes a partial auto-routing algorithm based on morphological operations of dilation and thinning to automate signal routing on PCBs. It covers escape and general routing in one layer, optimizing area usage and trace length.

articleTitle: Radiated Emissions of a CNC in a GTEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Nowadays portable Computer Numerical Control (CNC) Machines are very common as a tool for manufacturing parts or as positioners application in measurement systems. Its electromechanical components, such as motors and control electronics, are elements that emit electromagnetic fields into the environment that can interfere with other systems or with their own electronics systems. This paper presents the measurements of electromagnetic emissions (EMI) of a CNC with a 24 V DC spindle motor: 10000 r/min, two 12 V stepper motors with 1.3 A phase current, phase resistance of 2.1 Ohm with a torque of 0.25 Nm, The EMI measurement was performed inside a Gigahertz Transverse Electromagnetic (GTEM) cell, which are correlated to the far field prediction for 3, 10 and 30 m, corresponding to an open area test site (OATS) or an anechoic chamber. The results show that in the near field the emissions are higher than 80 dBμV/m below 200MHz and 25 dBμV/m above 350 MHz.

articleTitle: Design of -45°Constant BP-NGD Microwave Phase Shifter Using LCL T-Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: An application of unfamiliar bandpass (BP) negative group delay (NGD) circuit for designing microwave passive phase shifter (PS) is introduced. The constant PS is designed by using positive group delay (PGD) circuit represented by LCL network and BP-NGD function. The RLC-parallel network constituted the PS BP-NGD topology. The theory of BP-NGD constant PS is established based on the S-parameters modelling. The BP-NGD synthesis equations are formulated in function of the design goals noticed by desired PS value P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>=-45° and center frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>=1 GHz and 20 dB reflection loss. The theoretical design of the proposed BP-NGD PS is validated by comparison between the calculated and simulated results showing ΔP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>=+/-2.33° with bandwidth Δf=0.334 GHz. The insertion loss of the designed PS proof-of-concept is less than 2 dB. The investigated BP-NGD PS is potentially useful in the near future for the 6G antenna array integrated circuit design.

articleTitle: A Time-Domain Vector Network Analyzer Suitable to Characterize Passive and Active Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This work presents the implementation of a Time-Domain Vector Network Analyzer (TD-VNA) that measures the S-parameters of passive and active devices using the time-domain waveform of the incident and reflected voltages measured with an oscilloscope. The calibration of the TD-VNA is fully compatible with traditional calibration techniques used in a Vector Network Analyzer. The proposed TD-VNA can measure small and large-signal S-parameters of a transistor, as well as the transistor's gain compression and output power and the magnitude and relative phase of the transistor's output spectral components, the latter being a feature not available in commercial VNAs. Experimental data from a microstrip low-pass filter and a GaAs FET ATF34143 measured with the TD-VNA and with conventional test systems show a correlation higher than 99.5%

articleTitle: Radome Effects on X-band Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This article presents an analysis of the effects of radomes on the performance of X-band horn antennas. The return loss, gain and beamwidth values of the antenna are systematically analyzed as a function of radome design parameters such as complex permittivity, thickness, curvature and distance from the antenna. The analysis is performed through electromagnetic simulation using the finite element method. The results show that the return loss of the horn antenna in the X-band is significantly affected by the thickness of the radome, and therefore, the design parameter must be chosen based on the operating frequency of the antenna. Furthermore, the presence of the radome also affects the antenna gain and beamwidth values. These findings provide valuable information to improve the performance of the antenna in the presence of dielectric radome.

articleTitle: FNNs Models for Regression of S-Parameters in Multilayer Interconnects with Different Electrical Lengths
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Neural Networks are often used for classification problems, where the electrical system must meet certain specification or performance metrics by selecting the appropriate input parameters or features. However, in many scenarios, the full response of the system is required, for instance, in terms of S-parameters in the frequency domain. Learning this continuous system response is a non-trivial task. An efficient regression model needs to learn from the training data sampled at different frequency points. In this paper, a feed-forward neural network as a predictive S-parameter response model of multilayer interconnects is proposed. Hyperparameter optimization by genetic algorithms is employed, and it was found that the model complexity (number of trainable parameters) increases for longer maximum electrical lengths of the transmission. Therefore, it becomes increasingly difficult to derive a good prediction with long electrical lengths that covers all the frequency range of interest.

articleTitle: Multilayer Additively Manufactured X-Band Electromagnetic Coupling Structure for Detachable Wireless Antenna Feed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: As additive manufacturing technologies evolve and allow for easier conformal printing of 3D antennas, functional surfaces are used for both mechanical and electrical functions. E.g., a UAV wing can be used as both a flight surface and an antenna. These conformal antennas tend to have the radiation elements on the outer surfaces of the structures and the feed port on the inner surfaces. Using electric connections between the layers adds points for electric and mechanical failures, as these structures are subject to external forces and temperature cycles. This paper presents the concept of a wireless antenna feed, where a detachable electromagnetic coupling structure is used to feed the outer antenna element from the inner structure surface. Flat wireless feed prototypes with both, commercial microwave laminates and additive manufacturing are designed, manufactured, and tested for the 8–9 GHz band.

articleTitle: Compact Filtering Power Divider with Low Insertion Loss for GNSS Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a two-way filtering power divider for Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) receivers. The implemented device has a bandpass response suitable for selecting the L1 band signals of GPS and GLONASS, which are used in the majority of the commercial receivers. The proposed architecture is a modification of the microstrip Wilkinson power divider to provide filtering without significantly increasing the area required for its implementation. Therefore, it allows to replace two discrete components typically used in GNSS receivers with one integrated device, reducing the cost and the size of the circuits. Measurements carried out to the fabricated prototype show that bandpass filtering characteristics are attained with a typical insertion loss of about 3.5 dB and good impedance matching at all ports. articleTitle: Application of Software Defined Radio Technology for Low-Cost Characterization of Frequency-Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Frequency-Selective Surfaces (FSSs) are a promising tool for dealing with electromagnetic compatibility challenges in smart cities. While FSS prototypes demand a small investment, their characterization usually involves expensive radio frequency generators and analyzers. Here, we propose an FSS characterization setup based on Soft Defined Radio (SDR) technology as a low-cost alternative. To experimentally validate the proposed configuration, we employed it to characterize an example FSS in the 2.4 GHz band, comparing the results with those obtained using a signal generator and a spectrum analyzer. The setups provided a comparable performance, with maximum and mean squared transmission differences below 2 dB and 0.5 dB, respectively. Although slower and less sensitive, the SDR setup is portable and almost 50 times cheaper.

articleTitle: Two-Ray Model Analysis for Overwater Communication at 28 GHz with Different Heights
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This research aims to assess the signal propagation behavior of millimeter waves (mmWaves) over maritime environments. It focuses on the path loss performance of shore-to-vessel and vessel-to-vessel overwater communication at 28 GHz when considering line-of-sight conditions. The study is conducted by means of synthetic simulations at four different receiver antenna heights with respect to the water surface, representing emerging maritime Internet-of-Things application scenarios. Simulation results are shown concerning the path loss and the excess path loss - additional path loss relative to that in free-space - for each particular antenna height, over different TX-RX separations. We also show the cumulative distribution function of the excess path loss. The outcomes reveal variations of up to 10 dB in path loss performance depending on the height-distance setup. The results also reveal an initial distance range for all antenna heights in which the excess path loss is below 3 dB with 90% probability.

articleTitle: EMI Mitigation Enabled by a Printed Dipole Antenna with Composite Right/Left-Handed (CRLH) Structure: A Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: In high-density integrated systems where active systems like radar coexist with passive systems like radio direction finding, electromagnetic interference (EMI) from each antenna poses serious challenges to system integration. This paper demonstrates a CRLH-based dipole antenna that provides wideband operation at the operating frequency and significantly suppresses higher-order modes in the interference band, thereby reducing system EMI. In a demonstration experiment, an operating frequency equivalent to 80% of the relative bandwidth was obtained, exhibiting dipole antenna-like behavior and achieving a maximum of 5.71 dBi. Additionally, sensitivity suppression of less than -4.64 dBi was observed in all directions within the interference band.

articleTitle: New Design of Metamaterial Absorber for Electromagnetic Shielding in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) issues in electric vehicles have attracted attention in recent years. Internationally renowned automobile manufacturers consider EMC technology to be a very important technology for electric vehicles. Solving the EMC problem and facing this challenge has become the key to ensuring vehicle safety and reducing and preventing failures. In this context, to protect on-board and off-board receivers from electromagnetic interference, the periodic structures of resonator rings, known as Split Ring Resonators (SRR), have shown promise in mitigating these disadvantages. This paper presents the performance of a periodic structure of square, circular, and triangular distributed Split Ring Resonators (SRR) on varied dielectric substrates. Simulations and software optimization were carried out, seeking maximum absorption, with perspectives of application in electric vehicles. The structure analysis was performed in the range of 0 to 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Passive Resistorless Negative Group Delay Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: The negative group delay circuits, with its counterintuitive and promising behavior, have for most cases two main drawbacks: the bandwidth of negative group delay shows signal amplitude attenuation; and limited bandwidth. On this paper, a novel model to increase the bandwidth of the NGD circuits based on fully distributed circuits is presented. This model presented a 3.22% bandwidth at 2.45 GHz with a -6.11 dB minimum S21 and a -1.76 ns maximum NGD. Its flat response region comprises a 1.59% bandwidth with a 79.54% quality factor.

articleTitle: Operation of Rigid-Flex 3-D Printed Microwave Antennas for UWB Radar Under Thermal and Vibration Stress Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: We present the application of novel additively manufactured hybrid rigid-flex Vivaldi antennas as transmit and receive elements for an ultra-wideband (UWB) frequency modulated continuous wave (FM-CW) radar. This paper focuses on a series of measurements performed at Ku-band (12–18 GHz) to assess the effectiveness of these 3- D printed antennas within the radar loop, under thermal and vibration stresses. First, we verified the antennas' satisfactory operation down to -32 °C and inferred that thermal cycling would have minimal effect on the impulse response of the radar system. Next, we investigated the effects and bounds of vibration stress that could be sustained by these antennas and offer recommendations to support even higher vibration levels in future design iterations. Additionally, we present a succinct overview of the antenna design and the experimental setup used to perform these measurements.

articleTitle: Bias Tee Design for RF Power Amplifiers and GaN FETs Characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for designing a biastee (BT) specifically tailored to characterize power Gallium Nitride (GaN) Field-Effect Transistors (FETs) and develop power amplifiers (PAs). The approach involves carefully selecting network components to ensure stability for conditionally stable FETs, a crucial factor in FET characterization and PA design. The proposed design methodology was validated by designing two BTs to characterize the CGH40006P GaN FET from 0.1 to 6 GHz. The S-parameters measurements using the custom-fabricated BTs were compared to two commercial BTs: one prone to autonomous oscillation and the other without such oscillation tendencies. This comparison confirms the effectiveness and suitability of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: A Class-F Power Amplifier Design Using a Commercial Nonlinear Embedding Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: A 30 W Class-F Power Amplifier at 2 GHz is designed using a new commercial Angelov embedding model. The prototype Power Amplifier designed is verified in EM simulation using the normal Angelov model to provide an output peak power of 45 dBm with 71 percent drain efficiency. A prototype PA has been fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Comparison of LiDAR and RGB Sensor Technologies Applied to Close-Range Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE MTT-S Latin America Microwave Conference (LAMC)
abstract: This paper discusses methodological and quality aspects of photogrammetric products using high-resolution RGB and LiDAR sensors to derive 3D panoramas with rich multilevel spatial information. The comparative analysis from the two sensing approaches confirms that the RGB sensor in the visible region enables a colorful description of surface models, whereas the LiDAR sensor in the infrared region provides exceptional scene reconstruction capabilities with high levels of detail and accuracy. Through a case study of a rural landscape with partial forest coverage in Costa Rica, the advantages, and disadvantages of the two remote sensing principles are discussed and compared.
